question:
In the process of bisecting angle BAC in the given figure, why do we draw arcs from points D and E?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be0e88b64aa4e2dee550bd04cb0643dc30db9da8b75c837dd59bb10d6a918d5f.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __To intersect above A.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Drawing arcs from points D and E__ is an essential step in bisecting an angle.
 
• This action ensures that the arcs intersect at a point above A, which is crucial for accurate angle bisection.
 
• The intersection point allows the construction of a line that divides the angle into two equal parts.
 
• The method ensures precision and eliminates errors in manual angle bisection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance of Arcs in Geometry:**

 
 
• Arcs are used to create reference points for geometric constructions.
 
• They ensure accuracy and consistency in dividing angles, segments, or shapes.
 
 
 
• **Steps in Angle Bisection:**
 
 
• Identify the angle to be bisected.
 
• Draw arcs from the vertex and intersections on the angle's arms.
 
• Mark the intersection point of these arcs above the angle.
 
• Connect the vertex to this intersection point for perfect bisection.
